newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court keeps anti-dumping duty on cotton yarn.
newsitem.headline: Court keeps anti-dumping duty on cotton yarn.

text.p: The European Court of Justice upheld on Thursday anti-dumping duties imposed on cotton yarn imports into the European Union from Brazil and Turkey.
The court explained that Community rules provide for increases in anti-dumping duties on imports of cotton yarn to be paid under financing agreements more than 30 days after delivery within the EU.

The increase in duties is to be based on the actual price paid under a financing agreement, less charges for interest on deferred payment. The interest charged must be based on prevailing rates to prevent operators from artificially reducing the basis for assessment, the court said.
Reference for a preliminary ruling by the Supremo Tribunal Administrativo between
on the interpretation of article 1(3) of Council regulation (EEC) No 738/92 imposing a definitive anti-dumping duty on imports of cotton yarn originating in Brazil and Turkey (OJ 1992 L 82, p. 1)

The increase provided for in article 1(3) of Council regulation (EEC) No 738/92 imposing a definitive anti-dumping duty on imports of cotton yarn originating in Brazil and Turkey must be applied whenever it is agreed that imported goods are to be paid for more than 30 days after their arrival in the customs territory of the Community, even where the difference between the price for deferred payment and that for payment CAD is greater, in percentage terms, than the increase to be applied.
